holidays.name: National Old Stuff Day
holidays.description: A day to dig out the things you've been hanging onto, like the vintage record player, the lumpy sweater and the box of mystery cables, and give them some love. You can also use it to rediscover, repair, donate or finally admit you'll never use them again.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among thrifters, antique hunters and declutterers.
holidays.funFact: Many people use the day as a reason to visit flea markets and antique shops, so one person's old stuff becomes another person's treasure.

holidays.name: National Banana Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A salute to the creamy, dreamy dessert of banana slices, vanilla custard and whipped topping in a flaky or crumb crust. It's an excuse to eat pie in the name of tradition.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands on March 2 in holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Banana cream pie is a classic of American diners, and it is a staple of the pie-in-the-face gag in slapstick comedy.

holidays.name: Read Across America Day
holidays.description: A nationwide celebration of reading that encourages kids and grown-ups to pick up a book. Schools and libraries mark it with storytimes, costumes and a lot of green eggs and ham.
holidays.origin: The National Education Association launched it in 1998 to promote childhood literacy. It is held on March 2, the birthday of Dr. Seuss (Theodor Seuss Geisel), who was born in 1904.
holidays.funFact: Dr. Seuss wrote The Cat in the Hat using a list of only 236 simple words, after a challenge to write a book young readers couldn't put down.
